title: Amazon SES: sending email at scale

kcs.statement: Amazon SES sends transactional, marketing and bulk email at scale (and can receive email), with deliverability features such as DKIM signing and sender-reputation tracking.
For customised email to customers, such as HTML receipts or newsletters, choose SES; for simple alert notifications to subscribed endpoints, including email, choose SNS.

problem_ideas: An online shop must send 200,000 personalised HTML order confirmations a day: SES or SNS?
A new SES account cannot email customers: explain the sandbox and verified-identity restriction.
Ops wants an email when CPU passes 90%: which service sends it?
Rank three bounce/complaint scenarios by their effect on sender reputation.
Spot the distractor: 'Amazon Connect sends marketing email campaigns.'
A newsletter goes to spam folders; name the SES feature that proves the domain sent it.
